name: Macimorelin
lead: Macimorelin (brand name Macrilen) is an orally active ghrelin-receptor agonist that stimulates release of growth hormone. It is approved by the US FDA as a diagnostic test for adult growth hormone deficiency (AGHD), not as a treatment.[1][2]

In the test, a single oral dose is given and growth hormone levels are measured afterwards. Trials compared it with the insulin tolerance test and with arginine plus GHRH testing.[3][4][5] The US label lists QT prolongation among its warnings.[2]
No studies have tested macimorelin for appearance or muscle-building purposes. It appears in looksmaxxing-adjacent discussion only as one of the ghrelin-mimetic growth hormone secretagogues.
infobox: Aeterna Zentaris; rights held by Novo Nordisk 2018-2022[1]

paras: The US label indicates macrilen for the diagnosis of adult growth hormone deficiency. Its safety and diagnostic performance have not been established in people with a body mass index above 40.[2] Wikipedia describes it as the first oral test of its kind, as other stimulation tests such as the insulin tolerance test are given by injection and the insulin tolerance test can cause severe hypoglycemia.[1][3]

Macimorelin activates growth hormone secretagogue receptors in the pituitary and hypothalamus, triggering growth hormone release.[2] In healthy volunteers it also affected other pituitary hormones, including copeptin and oxytocin, in small studies.[6][7]
The drug is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4 in the liver; the label cautions that strong CYP3A4 inducers can cause false-positive results.[1][2]

The most common reactions listed on the US label include altered taste, dizziness, headache, fatigue, nausea, hunger, diarrhea and upper respiratory infection.[2] The label warns of QT-interval prolongation of about 11 msec and advises avoiding other QT-prolonging drugs.[2] No pregnancy data are available, but use is single-dose.[2]

A multicentre open-label study validated macimorelin against arginine plus GHRH testing for AGHD.[3] A later study compared it with the insulin tolerance test, and further analyses reported its sensitivity and specificity.[4][5] A pediatric phase 3 study was also registered.[8] Pilot work tested repeated doses in cancer cachexia in 15 patients.[9]

Expert reviews discuss it as one option in diagnosing AGHD, and a Delphi survey of the Growth Hormone Research Society covered consensus and controversies about diagnosis.[10][11] No studies were found in healthy people for appearance outcomes.

Macimorelin was first synthesised through a collaboration involving the University of Montpellier, the CNRS and Aeterna Zentaris, and the FDA approved it in December 2017.[1] Novo Nordisk bought the rights in November 2018 for 145 million US dollars and returned them to Aeterna Zentaris in 2022.[1]

timeline.event: Validation study of oral macimorelin test for AGHD published.[3]
FDA approves Macrilen as a diagnostic.[1]

card.summary: Oral ghrelin-receptor agonist approved only as a one-time diagnostic for adult GH deficiency; nothing on looks.
card.note: Approved only as a diagnostic test; label warns of QT prolongation.

quick.overview:
Macimorelin is a prescription drug sold as Macrilen. Doctors give it once, by mouth, to see whether the pituitary releases enough growth hormone, which helps diagnose adult growth hormone deficiency.

It was approved in the US in December 2017. It is not approved as a treatment and no study has tested it for appearance.
quick.mechanism: It binds the ghrelin (GH secretagogue) receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, which prompts a pulse of growth hormone that can be measured.
quick.risks: The label lists altered taste, dizziness, headache and nausea as common reactions and warns of QT prolongation. Strong CYP3A4 inducers can distort test results.
